description: Simulated three-market customer evidence for one synthetic vehicle: CN wants more rear space and a quieter cabin, US wants a louder exhaust, EU is balanced. Connectivity is the control topic and must produce no conflict. Not BMW data.

design.note: Each market's six topics get 6..1 records, so the deterministic reference pipeline (customer_impact = min(5, 1.5 + log2(1 + n) / 3), other factors constant) ranks topics by record count without ties. With six topics, 'top third' is ranks 1-2 and 'bottom half' is ranks 4-6 (PLATFORM_BUILD_PLAN.md Pod B priority_divergence). Every market has evidence on every topic, so no evidence_gap is expected; all deterministic targets are identical, so no target_incompatible is expected.
design.direction_terms: Only CN quietness records say 'quieter' and only US driving-experience records say 'louder' (exhaust); no other record uses louder/quieter, softer/firmer, bigger/smaller or compact.

gold_conflicts.rationale: CN asks for a quieter cabin while US asks for a louder exhaust: the quietness vs driving-experience/exhaust-sound tension pair.
Comfort (rear space) ranks 1 of 6 in CN and 6 of 6 in US.
Driving experience (exhaust sound) ranks 1 of 6 in US and 6 of 6 in CN and EU.
